title: 1952 AHSME Problem 12
statement: The sum to infinity of the terms of an infinite geometric progression is \(6.\) The sum of the first two terms is \(4\dfrac12.\) The first term of the progression is:

solutions.text:
Let the first term be \(a\) and the common ratio be \(r.\) The infinite sum gives \(a=6(1-r).\) The first two terms therefore satisfy \[ a(1+r)=6(1-r^2)=\frac92. \] Thus \(r^2=\frac{1}{4},\) so \(r=\frac{1}{2}\) gives \(a=3,\) while \(r=-\frac{1}{2}\) gives \(a=9.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
